This market and these products have not been endorsed by the Primary Source Agency or its affiliates. Any references to the Primary Source Agency’s delay and cancellation page, or any associated marks are descriptive only and do not indicate an endorsement of this product or any affiliation between the Primary Source Agency or its affiliates and Kalshi.

EXCLUDED EVENTS

“Excluded Event” means any event or circumstance arising from, or directly resulting from:

(i) Any act of unlawful interference with civil aviation, including sabotage, unlawful seizure of aircraft, or interference with air navigation facilities or services;

(ii) Any deliberate act or omission by any person, whether or not identified, undertaken with the purpose or reasonably foreseeable effect of disrupting operations at John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK/KJFK), including without limitation unauthorized unmanned aircraft operations, laser illumination, trespass upon or unauthorized presence within the air operations area, tampering with or destruction of airport, air carrier, air traffic control, or utility infrastructure serving John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK/KJFK), and false reports or threats resulting in evacuation, ground stop, or suspension of operations;

(iii) Any malicious cyber incident affecting systems of John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK/KJFK), any air carrier, or any air navigation service provider, as characterized by the affected entity or a governmental authority; or

(iv) Any security-related closure, ground stop, or operational suspension ordered by a governmental authority in response to an actual or suspected act described in clauses (i)–(iii) or to any actual or suspected act of unlawful violence, wherever occurring.

HOW THE CANCELLATION PERCENTAGE IS CALCULATED

The cancellation percentage is calculated by dividing the number of cancelled flights within the fixed schedule by the total number of scheduled flights and multiplying the result by 100. The result is carried to two decimal places without rounding; any digits beyond the second decimal place are truncated.

Schedule baseline: The schedule baseline for this market is October 19, 2026 at 11:59:59 PM ET.

Fixed scheduled-flight total: The binding total number of scheduled flights will be determined as of October 19, 2026 at 11:59:59 PM ET. This total consists of commercial passenger and cargo flights, including arrivals and departures combined, scheduled to operate at John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK/KJFK) during October 21, 2026.

The fixed total includes any flight subsequently cancelled and is not reduced by cancellations, schedule changes, or removals occurring after the schedule baseline. Flights added after the schedule baseline are excluded from both the scheduled-flight total and the cancellation count.

Cancelled flights: A flight counts as cancelled only if it is included in the fixed scheduled-flight total and is classified as cancelled by the Primary Source Agency as of the Expiration time. Cancellations made after the schedule baseline but before the beginning of October 21, 2026, including pre-emptive cancellations, are counted.

Reinstated flights: A flight initially classified as cancelled that is subsequently reinstated and operates during October 21, 2026 is not counted as cancelled.

Excluded flight outcomes: Delayed flights, diverted flights, and gate returns that ultimately depart are not counted as cancelled, regardless of the length of the delay.

Corrections and revisions: Corrections, retractions, or restatements made by the Primary Source Agency before Expiration will be considered. Revisions made after Expiration will not be considered.

Local time and flight attribution: All dates and times relating to the scheduling and operation of flights are interpreted in the local time of John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK/KJFK) unless otherwise specified. Each flight is attributed to October 21, 2026 according to its originally scheduled date of operation at the airport.

AIRPORT CLOSURE

If John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK/KJFK) is fully closed and no scheduled flight operates for the entirety of October 21, 2026, the cancellation percentage will be deemed 100.00%.

If the scheduled-flight total is zero because the airport is closed, or has been ordered or announced to be closed, for the entirety of October 21, 2026, the cancellation percentage will be deemed 100.00%. If the scheduled-flight total is zero for any other reason, the outcome will be determined pursuant to Rule 7.1 of the Rulebook.

template: This market resolves to Yes if any Source Agency confirms that one or more Nvidia H# chips have been physically delivered to, received in, or imported into mainland China after Issuance and before <M> # #. For this market, “mainland China” means the People’s Republic of China excluding Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan. Delivery to Hong Kong, Macau, or Taiwan does not qualify unless a Source Agency confirms that the Nvidia H# chips were subsequently delivered to, received in, or imported into mainland China. Regulatory approval, export licenses, purchase orders, contracts, reservations, customer allocations, payment, revenue-recognition statements, manufacturing, packaging, shipment preparation, or statements of intent do not qualify unless a Source Agency confirms physical delivery, receipt, or import into mainland China. References to Nvidia “H#” “H# AI chips,” “H# GPUs,” “H# processors,” “H# accelerators,” or “H# AI accelerators” qualify, provided the Source Agency is referring to Nvidia H# chips. References only to other Nvidia chips, including H# H# B# B# Blackwell, or China-specific modified chips, do not qualify unless the Source Agency also confirms delivery of Nvidia H# chips. A report that Nvidia H# chips were delivered to an approved Chinese customer outside mainland China will not qualify, unless a Source Agency confirms that those chips were delivered to, received in, or imported into mainland China before <M> # #.
raw:
This market resolves to Yes if any Source Agency confirms that one or more Nvidia H200 chips have been physically delivered to, received in, or imported into mainland China after Issuance and before Jan. 1, 2027.

For this market, “mainland China” means the People’s Republic of China excluding Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan. Delivery to Hong Kong, Macau, or Taiwan does not qualify unless a Source Agency confirms that the Nvidia H200 chips were subsequently delivered to, received in, or imported into mainland China.

Regulatory approval, export licenses, purchase orders, contracts, reservations, customer allocations, payment, revenue-recognition statements, manufacturing, packaging, shipment preparation, or statements of intent do not qualify unless a Source Agency confirms physical delivery, receipt, or import into mainland China.

References to Nvidia “H200,” “H200 AI chips,” “H200 GPUs,” “H200 processors,” “H200 accelerators,” or “H200 AI accelerators” qualify, provided the Source Agency is referring to Nvidia H200 chips. References only to other Nvidia chips, including H20, H100, B200, B300, Blackwell, or China-specific modified chips, do not qualify unless the Source Agency also confirms delivery of Nvidia H200 chips.

A report that Nvidia H200 chips were delivered to an approved Chinese customer outside mainland China will not qualify, unless a Source Agency confirms that those chips were delivered to, received in, or imported into mainland China before Jan. 1, 2027.

template: If the first calendar day in the ## winter season on which Copper Mountain Resort conducts Seasonal Opening Operations occurs before <M> # # then the market resolves to Yes.
raw: If the first calendar day in the 2026-27 winter season on which Copper Mountain Resort conducts Seasonal Opening Operations occurs before Oct 25, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.

template: How this is resolved Seasonal Opening Operations require at least one passenger lift to carry members of the general public uphill for downhill skiing or snowboarding on terrain designated open for that use by Copper Mountain Resort. The opening calendar day is determined in Eastern Time. The season runs from <M> # through <M> # of the following year. “Before” excludes the specified date. A name, branding, ownership, operator, or website change does not change the resort’s geographic identity. If no Source Agency has documented Seasonal Opening Operations by expiration and there is insufficient information to determine their occurrence, the market resolves to last fair price, as determined by the Exchange in its sole discretion. If Copper Mountain Resort is decommissioned, the market resolves to No. Payout criteria Access counts only when holders of a season pass valid for the specified season can use those lifts and terrain without an additional purchase. Free reservations and passholder-only days count. Any number of lifts, any amount of terrain, and any operating duration count. Doesn’t count for payout Employee, contractor, invited-media, private-event, and separately purchased early-access or preview days do not count. Scenic rides, mountain biking, hiking, tubing, and uphill-only access do not count. Scheduled, projected, or announced opening dates do not count. Kalshi is not affiliated, associated, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with the Copper Mountain Resort. All trademarks, logos, and brand names are the property of their respective owners.
raw:
How this is resolved
Seasonal Opening Operations require at least one passenger lift to carry members of the general public uphill for downhill skiing or snowboarding on terrain designated open for that use by Copper Mountain Resort.
The opening calendar day is determined in Eastern Time.
The season runs from September 1 through August 31 of the following year. “Before” excludes the specified date.  
A name, branding, ownership, operator, or website change does not change the resort’s geographic identity.
If no Source Agency has documented Seasonal Opening Operations by expiration and there is insufficient information to determine their occurrence, the market resolves to last fair price, as determined by the Exchange in its sole discretion.
If Copper Mountain Resort is decommissioned, the market resolves to No.

Payout criteria
Access counts only when holders of a season pass valid for the specified season can use those lifts and terrain without an additional purchase.
Free reservations and passholder-only days count.
Any number of lifts, any amount of terrain, and any operating duration count.

Doesn’t count for payout
Employee, contractor, invited-media, private-event, and separately purchased early-access or preview days do not count.
Scenic rides, mountain biking, hiking, tubing, and uphill-only access do not count.
Scheduled, projected, or announced opening dates do not count.

Kalshi is not affiliated, associated, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with the Copper Mountain Resort. All trademarks, logos, and brand names are the property of their respective owners.

template: How this is resolved Seasonal Opening Operations require at least one passenger lift to carry members of the general public uphill for downhill skiing or snowboarding on terrain designated open for that use by Copper Mountain Resort. The opening calendar day is determined in Eastern Time. The season runs from <M> # through <M> # of the following year. “Before” excludes the specified date. A name, branding, ownership, operator, or website change does not change the resort’s geographic identity. If no Source Agency has documented Seasonal Opening Operations by expiration and there is insufficient information to determine their occurrence, the market resolves to last fair price, as determined by the Exchange in its sole discretion. If Copper Mountain Resort is decommissioned, the market resolves to No. Payout criteria Access counts only when holders of a season pass valid for the specified season can use those lifts and terrain without an additional purchase. Free reservations and passholder-only days count. Any number of lifts, any amount of terrain, and any operating duration count. Doesn’t count for payout Employee, contractor, invited-media, private-event, and separately purchased early-access or preview days do not count. Scenic rides, mountain biking, hiking, tubing, and uphill-only access do not count. Scheduled, projected, or announced opening dates do not count. Kalshi is not affiliated, associated, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with the Copper Mountain Resort. All trademarks, logos, and brand names are the property of their respective owners.
raw:
How this is resolved
Seasonal Opening Operations require at least one passenger lift to carry members of the general public uphill for downhill skiing or snowboarding on terrain designated open for that use by Copper Mountain Resort.
The opening calendar day is determined in Eastern Time.
The season runs from September 1 through August 31 of the following year. “Before” excludes the specified date.  
A name, branding, ownership, operator, or website change does not change the resort’s geographic identity.
If no Source Agency has documented Seasonal Opening Operations by expiration and there is insufficient information to determine their occurrence, the market resolves to last fair price, as determined by the Exchange in its sole discretion.
If Copper Mountain Resort is decommissioned, the market resolves to No.

Payout criteria
Access counts only when holders of a season pass valid for the specified season can use those lifts and terrain without an additional purchase.
Free reservations and passholder-only days count.
Any number of lifts, any amount of terrain, and any operating duration count.

Doesn’t count for payout
Employee, contractor, invited-media, private-event, and separately purchased early-access or preview days do not count.
Scenic rides, mountain biking, hiking, tubing, and uphill-only access do not count.
Scheduled, projected, or announced opening dates do not count.

Kalshi is not affiliated, associated, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with the Copper Mountain Resort. All trademarks, logos, and brand names are the property of their respective owners.

template: How this is resolved Seasonal Opening Operations require at least one passenger lift to carry members of the general public uphill for downhill skiing or snowboarding on resort-designated open terrain. The opening calendar day is determined in Eastern Time. A name, owner, operator, or website change does not change the resort's identity. If the ski resort is decommissioned, the market resolves to No. Payout criteria Season-passholder-only access counts if it requires no additional purchase. Any number of lifts, any amount of terrain, and any operating duration count. If its terrain is split across separately operated areas, opening any portion counts. Doesn't count for payout Employee, contractor, invited-media, private-event, and separately purchased early-access or preview days do not count. Scenic rides, mountain biking, hiking, tubing, and uphill-only access do not count. Announced or projected dates do not count. Kalshi is not affiliated, associated, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with the resort. All trademarks, logos, and brand names are the property of their respective owners.
raw:
How this is resolved
Seasonal Opening Operations require at least one passenger lift to carry members of the general public uphill for downhill skiing or snowboarding on resort-designated open terrain. 
The opening calendar day is determined in Eastern Time.
A name, owner, operator, or website change does not change the resort's identity.
If the ski resort is decommissioned, the market resolves to No.

Payout criteria
Season-passholder-only access counts if it requires no additional purchase.

template: How this is resolved Seasonal Opening Operations require at least one passenger lift to carry members of the general public uphill for downhill skiing or snowboarding on resort-designated open terrain. The opening calendar day is determined in Eastern Time. A name, owner, operator, or website change does not change the resort's identity. If the ski resort is decommissioned, the market resolves to No. Payout criteria Season-passholder-only access counts if it requires no additional purchase. Any number of lifts, any amount of terrain, and any operating duration count. If its terrain is split across separately operated areas, opening any portion counts. Doesn't count for payout Employee, contractor, invited-media, private-event, and separately purchased early-access or preview days do not count. Scenic rides, mountain biking, hiking, tubing, and uphill-only access do not count. Announced or projected dates do not count. Kalshi is not affiliated, associated, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with the resort. All trademarks, logos, and brand names are the property of their respective owners.

template: A track segment is the straight line connecting the storm positions in two consecutive official National Hurricane Center public or forecast advisories. The named storm is Isaias in the # season; the cutoff is the stated calendar date, not the end of the usual hurricane season. Unofficial coordinates and post-storm analyses do not establish a qualifying track segment, and revisions after expiration are disregarded. Trading closes <M> # # at #:# PM EST. The latest expiration is <M> # # at #:# AM EST; expiration may move earlier after a qualifying occurrence in accordance with Rule #. Settlement is no later than the day after expiration unless the outcome is under review pursuant to Rule #. The HURPATH outcome-review and indeterminacy provisions remain applicable.
raw: A track segment is the straight line connecting the storm positions in two consecutive official National Hurricane Center public or forecast advisories. A segment qualifies if any part of that line passes through the defined region, or either coordinate point lies within it. The region is the Alabama feature (STATEFP 01, STUSPS AL) in the US Census Bureau 2025 cartographic boundary state shapefile at 1:500,000 scale: https://www2.census.gov/geo/tiger/GENZ2025/shp/cb2025usstate500k.zip . This is a track-intersection test; a coastal landfall in Alabama is not required. The named storm is Isaias in the 2026 season; the cutoff is the stated calendar date, not the end of the usual hurricane season. Unofficial coordinates and post-storm analyses do not establish a qualifying track segment, and revisions after expiration are disregarded. Trading closes December 30, 2026 at 11:59 PM EST. The latest expiration is January 7, 2027 at 10:00 AM EST; expiration may move earlier after a qualifying occurrence in accordance with Rule 7.2. Settlement is no later than the day after expiration unless the outcome is under review pursuant to Rule 7.1. The HURPATH outcome-review and indeterminacy provisions remain applicable.

template: How this is resolved Seasonal Opening Operations require at least one passenger lift to carry members of the general public uphill for downhill skiing or snowboarding on resort-designated open terrain. The opening calendar day is determined in Eastern Time. A name, owner, operator, or website change does not change the resort's identity. If the ski resort is decommissioned, the market resolves to No. Payout criteria Season-passholder-only access counts if it requires no additional purchase. Any number of lifts, any amount of terrain, and any operating duration count. If its terrain is split across separately operated areas, opening any portion counts. Doesn't count for payout Employee, contractor, invited-media, private-event, and separately purchased early-access or preview days do not count. Scenic rides, mountain biking, hiking, tubing, and uphill-only access do not count. Announced or projected dates do not count. Kalshi is not affiliated, associated, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with the resort. All trademarks, logos, and brand names are the property of their respective owners.

template: How this is resolved Seasonal Opening Operations require at least one passenger lift to carry members of the general public uphill for downhill skiing or snowboarding on terrain designated open for that use by Killington Resort. The opening calendar day is determined in Eastern Time. The season runs from <M> # through <M> # of the following year. “Before” excludes the specified date. A name, branding, ownership, operator, or website change does not change the resort’s geographic identity. If no Source Agency has documented Seasonal Opening Operations by expiration and there is insufficient information to determine their occurrence, the market resolves to last fair price, as determined by the Exchange in its sole discretion. If Killington Resort is decommissioned, the market resolves to No. Payout criteria Access counts only when holders of a season pass valid for the specified season can use those lifts and terrain without an additional purchase. Free reservations and passholder-only days count. Any number of lifts, any amount of terrain, and any operating duration count. Only Killington Resort counts. Doesn’t count for payout Employee, contractor, invited-media, private-event, and separately purchased early-access or preview days do not count. Scenic rides, mountain biking, hiking, tubing, and uphill-only access do not count. Scheduled, projected, or announced opening dates do not count. Opening at Pico Mountain does not count. Kalshi is not affiliated, associated, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with the Killington Resort. All trademarks, logos, and brand names are the property of their respective owners.
raw:
How this is resolved
Seasonal Opening Operations require at least one passenger lift to carry members of the general public uphill for downhill skiing or snowboarding on terrain designated open for that use by Killington Resort.
The opening calendar day is determined in Eastern Time.
The season runs from September 1 through August 31 of the following year. “Before” excludes the specified date.
A name, branding, ownership, operator, or website change does not change the resort’s geographic identity.
If no Source Agency has documented Seasonal Opening Operations by expiration and there is insufficient information to determine their occurrence, the market resolves to last fair price, as determined by the Exchange in its sole discretion.
If Killington Resort is decommissioned, the market resolves to No.

Payout criteria
Access counts only when holders of a season pass valid for the specified season can use those lifts and terrain without an additional purchase.
Free reservations and passholder-only days count.
Any number of lifts, any amount of terrain, and any operating duration count.
Only Killington Resort counts.

Doesn’t count for payout
Employee, contractor, invited-media, private-event, and separately purchased early-access or preview days do not count.
Scenic rides, mountain biking, hiking, tubing, and uphill-only access do not count.
Scheduled, projected, or announced opening dates do not count. 
Opening at Pico Mountain does not count. 

Kalshi is not affiliated, associated, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with the Killington Resort. All trademarks, logos, and brand names are the property of their respective owners.

template: How this is resolved Seasonal Opening Operations require at least one passenger lift to carry members of the general public uphill for downhill skiing or snowboarding on resort-designated open terrain. The opening calendar day is determined in Eastern Time. A name, owner, operator, or website change does not change the resort's identity. If the ski resort is decommissioned, the market resolves to No. Payout criteria Season-passholder-only access counts if it requires no additional purchase. Any number of lifts, any amount of terrain, and any operating duration count. If its terrain is split across separately operated areas, opening any portion counts. Doesn't count for payout Employee, contractor, invited-media, private-event, and separately purchased early-access or preview days do not count. Scenic rides, mountain biking, hiking, tubing, and uphill-only access do not count. Announced or projected dates do not count. Kalshi is not affiliated, associated, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with Mammoth Mountain or Alterra Mountain Company. All trademarks, logos, and brand names are the property of their respective owners.

template: How this is resolved Seasonal Opening Operations require at least one passenger lift to carry members of the general public uphill for downhill skiing or snowboarding on resort-designated open terrain. The opening calendar day is determined in Eastern Time. A name, owner, operator, or website change does not change the resort's identity. If the ski resort is decommissioned, the market resolves to No. Payout criteria Season-passholder-only access counts if it requires no additional purchase. Any number of lifts, any amount of terrain, and any operating duration count. If its terrain is split across separately operated areas, opening any portion counts. Doesn't count for payout Employee, contractor, invited-media, private-event, and separately purchased early-access or preview days do not count. Scenic rides, mountain biking, hiking, tubing, and uphill-only access do not count. Announced or projected dates do not count. Kalshi is not affiliated, associated, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with the resort. All trademarks, logos, and brand names are the property of their respective owners.

If the ski resort is decommissioned, the market resolves to No.

Payout criteria

If its terrain is split across separately operated areas, opening any portion counts. 

Doesn't count for payout
Employee, contractor, invited-media, private-event, and separately purchased early-access or preview days do not count.
Scenic rides, mountain biking, hiking, tubing, and uphill-only access do not count.

template: A Millennium Prize Problem counts as solved on the first date that, by Expiration, remains unretracted and either: A complete proof, disproof, or counterexample addressing the problem as originally formulated by the Clay Mathematics Institute is published in a reputable peer-reviewed mathematics or scientific journal. CMI or another recognized academic governing or recognition body officially states that the problem has been resolved by reference to a specific written work. At least two Source Agencies themselves report that the problem has been proven, disproven, or otherwise resolved by reference to a specific publicly available written work. A preprint, announcement, blog post, conference presentation, technical report, or machine-checked formalization does NOT by itself constitute a solution, but may be the written work relied upon for official recognition or qualifying Source Agency reporting. Award of a Millennium Prize by CMI is NOT required. Partial results, special cases, unrelated reformulations, results conditional on unproven assumptions, and findings that the problem is independent of or undecidable within its framework do NOT count. The result must establish the truth or falsity of the problem as originally formulated. A solution is attributed to AI lab when Source Agencies report that AI lab, its personnel, or an AI system developed and operated by it produced the solution in whole or substantial part, and the lab or system is credited as an author, contributor, or producer. Collaborative work qualifies; independent third-party use of the lab's publicly available model or product without such participation or credit does NOT. Each Millennium Prize Problem counts at most once. Problems solved before time period do NOT count. A purported solution that is retracted, withdrawn, repudiated, rescinded, disavowed, or reported to contain an unresolved identified error before Expiration does NOT count.

template: The function must be live and processing user interactions, not explicitly labeled as "beta," "test," "experimental," "preview," or "early access" or similar, and officially acknowledged by the company through announcements, documentation, or help pages. Implementation includes direct integration into the product's interface, automatic application to user accounts, user-initiated activation through official controls, API implementation, or policy changes that operationally enforce the function. Announcements without deployment, employee-only testing, technical documentation without implementation, and third-party additions without authorization do not qualify. The implementation must occur in the United States unless otherwise specified. If it meets these conditions, it counts from the first date it is live for users outside the company, including in a gradual rollout or a waitlist, invitation-only, or paid-tier release. A general-purpose personal AI agent acts for an individual user on that user's own goals, is not limited to a single category of task or app, such as only code, only documents, or only shopping, and (#) retains user-specific information, such as preferences, relationships, goals, or ongoing activities, across separate interactions, and (#) as a built-in capability, on its own initiative and outside any conversation or task the user has started, begins new multi-step actions across third-party apps, websites, or services to advance the user's ongoing goals, based on what it has retained. The agent must itself take at least one such action before asking the user anything, and may then pause for approval before a step such as sending a message or making a purchase. An action means changing something in a third-party app, website, or service on the user's behalf, such as sending, posting, booking, purchasing, submitting a form, or creating, editing, or deleting an item; reading, searching, or summarizing does not count. An agent focused on work qualifies if it acts across email, calendar, messaging, and the web for an individual user. The following do not qualify: carrying out a task the user started, however long-running; running tasks on a user-defined schedule, event trigger, or monitor, or under a standing instruction that tells the agent what to do or which app, source, or workflow to watch; a briefing or notification on its own; a proposed task or suggestion that does nothing until the user accepts it; an offer made in reply to the user's message; memory alone; an agent configured by an organization to run shared team workflows; and a developer platform, SDK, or API for building agents, unless the company itself offers through it an agent that meets (#) and (#) for end users. A goal or preference the user has shared, from which the agent itself decides what new task to start, is not a standing instruction, and neither is turning the capability on, connecting apps, or granting permissions.
raw:
The function must be live and processing user interactions, not explicitly labeled as "beta," "test," "experimental," "preview," or "early access" or similar, and officially acknowledged by the company through announcements, documentation, or help pages. Implementation includes direct integration into the product's interface, automatic application to user accounts, user-initiated activation through official controls, API implementation, or policy changes that operationally enforce the function. Announcements without deployment, employee-only testing, technical documentation without implementation, and third-party additions without authorization do not qualify. The implementation must occur in the United States unless otherwise specified. If it meets these conditions, it counts from the first date it is live for users outside the company, including in a gradual rollout or a waitlist, invitation-only, or paid-tier release.

A general-purpose personal AI agent acts for an individual user on that user's own goals, is not limited to a single category of task or app, such as only code, only documents, or only shopping, and (1) retains user-specific information, such as preferences, relationships, goals, or ongoing activities, across separate interactions, and (2) as a built-in capability, on its own initiative and outside any conversation or task the user has started, begins new multi-step actions across third-party apps, websites, or services to advance the user's ongoing goals, based on what it has retained. The agent must itself take at least one such action before asking the user anything, and may then pause for approval before a step such as sending a message or making a purchase. An action means changing something in a third-party app, website, or service on the user's behalf, such as sending, posting, booking, purchasing, submitting a form, or creating, editing, or deleting an item; reading, searching, or summarizing does not count. An agent focused on work qualifies if it acts across email, calendar, messaging, and the web for an individual user.

The following do not qualify: carrying out a task the user started, however long-running; running tasks on a user-defined schedule, event trigger, or monitor, or under a standing instruction that tells the agent what to do or which app, source, or workflow to watch; a briefing or notification on its own; a proposed task or suggestion that does nothing until the user accepts it; an offer made in reply to the user's message; memory alone; an agent configured by an organization to run shared team workflows; and a developer platform, SDK, or API for building agents, unless the company itself offers through it an agent that meets (1) and (2) for end users. A goal or preference the user has shared, from which the agent itself decides what new task to start, is not a standing instruction, and neither is turning the capability on, connecting apps, or granting permissions.

Accelerated approval (based on surrogate endpoints)

template: The function must be live and processing user interactions, not explicitly labeled as "beta," "test," "experimental," "preview," or "early access" or similar, and officially acknowledged by the company through announcements, documentation, or help pages. Implementation includes direct integration into the product's interface, automatic application to user accounts, user-initiated activation through official controls, API implementation, or policy changes that operationally enforce the function. Announcements without deployment, employee-only testing, technical documentation without implementation, and third-party additions without authorization do not qualify. The implementation must occur in the United States unless otherwise specified. If it meets these conditions, it counts from the first date it is live for users outside the company, including in a gradual rollout or a waitlist, invitation-only, or paid-tier release. A general-purpose personal AI agent acts for an individual user on that user's own goals, is not limited to a single category of task or app, such as only code, only documents, or only shopping, and (#) retains user-specific information, such as preferences, relationships, goals, or ongoing activities, across separate interactions, and (#) as a built-in capability, on its own initiative and outside any conversation or task the user has started, begins new multi-step actions across third-party apps, websites, or services to advance the user's ongoing goals, based on what it has retained. The agent must itself take at least one such action before asking the user anything, and may then pause for approval before a step such as sending a message or making a purchase. An action means changing something in a third-party app, website, or service on the user's behalf, such as sending, posting, booking, purchasing, submitting a form, or creating, editing, or deleting an item; reading, searching, or summarizing does not count. An agent focused on work qualifies if it acts across email, calendar, messaging, and the web for an individual user. The following do not qualify: carrying out a task the user started, however long-running; running tasks on a user-defined schedule, event trigger, or monitor, or under a standing instruction that tells the agent what to do or which app, source, or workflow to watch; a briefing or notification on its own; a proposed task or suggestion that does nothing until the user accepts it; an offer made in reply to the user's message; memory alone; an agent configured by an organization to run shared team workflows; and a developer platform, SDK, or API for building agents, unless the company itself offers through it an agent that meets (#) and (#) for end users. A goal or preference the user has shared, from which the agent itself decides what new task to start, is not a standing instruction, and neither is turning the capability on, connecting apps, or granting permissions.
raw:
The function must be live and processing user interactions, not explicitly labeled as "beta," "test," "experimental," "preview," or "early access" or similar, and officially acknowledged by the company through announcements, documentation, or help pages. Implementation includes direct integration into the product's interface, automatic application to user accounts, user-initiated activation through official controls, API implementation, or policy changes that operationally enforce the function. Announcements without deployment, employee-only testing, technical documentation without implementation, and third-party additions without authorization do not qualify. The implementation must occur in the United States unless otherwise specified. If it meets these conditions, it counts from the first date it is live for users outside the company, including in a gradual rollout or a waitlist, invitation-only, or paid-tier release.

A general-purpose personal AI agent acts for an individual user on that user's own goals, is not limited to a single category of task or app, such as only code, only documents, or only shopping, and (1) retains user-specific information, such as preferences, relationships, goals, or ongoing activities, across separate interactions, and (2) as a built-in capability, on its own initiative and outside any conversation or task the user has started, begins new multi-step actions across third-party apps, websites, or services to advance the user's ongoing goals, based on what it has retained. The agent must itself take at least one such action before asking the user anything, and may then pause for approval before a step such as sending a message or making a purchase. An action means changing something in a third-party app, website, or service on the user's behalf, such as sending, posting, booking, purchasing, submitting a form, or creating, editing, or deleting an item; reading, searching, or summarizing does not count. An agent focused on work qualifies if it acts across email, calendar, messaging, and the web for an individual user.

The following do not qualify: carrying out a task the user started, however long-running; running tasks on a user-defined schedule, event trigger, or monitor, or under a standing instruction that tells the agent what to do or which app, source, or workflow to watch; a briefing or notification on its own; a proposed task or suggestion that does nothing until the user accepts it; an offer made in reply to the user's message; memory alone; an agent configured by an organization to run shared team workflows; and a developer platform, SDK, or API for building agents, unless the company itself offers through it an agent that meets (1) and (2) for end users. A goal or preference the user has shared, from which the agent itself decides what new task to start, is not a standing instruction, and neither is turning the capability on, connecting apps, or granting permissions.

template: For "offered to": Tesla has launched a robotaxi service in <S> that satisfies ALL of the following criteria: The service allows members of the general public to request rides through a publicly accessible application or platform (not limited to Tesla employees, beta testers, or invite-only participants) The vehicles operate without any human driver or safety monitor physically present in the driver's seat who is actively controlling the vehicle during normal operation The service charges fares or fees for rides (free promotional rides alone do not qualify) For "removed from": Tesla has discontinued, suspended, or withdrawn a previously operational robotaxi service in <S> that met all the "offered to" criteria above, where: The service is no longer accepting new ride requests from the general public for any period of time as a result of a decision by Tesla to suspend operations in the area, and such suspension is not explicitly characterized as temporary (e.g., due to weather, maintenance, or system upgrades). The Payout Criterion is not satisfied by short-term service interruptions that are clearly communicated as temporary or expected to resume. The following do NOT satisfy the Payout Criterion: If a government orders Tesla to cease ongoing services but they do not comply, then the market does not resolve to Yes Services limited to Tesla employees, contractors, or their guests Beta tests, pilot programs, or demonstrations Services requiring special invitations, access codes, or pre-approval to use Vehicles with human safety drivers, monitors, or operators in any seat of the vehicle who can take control Temporary suspensions due to weather or technical issues Services operating only with remote human teleoperators controlling each vehicle continuously Test fleets that are not charging fares to the general public Announcements of future launches without actual operational service
raw:
For "offered to": Tesla has launched a robotaxi service in Florida that satisfies ALL of the following criteria:

The service allows members of the general public to request rides through a publicly accessible application or platform (not limited to Tesla employees, beta testers, or invite-only participants)
The vehicles operate without any human driver or safety monitor physically present in the driver's seat who is actively controlling the vehicle during normal operation
The service charges fares or fees for rides (free promotional rides alone do not qualify)

For "removed from": Tesla has discontinued, suspended, or withdrawn a previously operational robotaxi service in Florida that met all the "offered to" criteria above, where:

The service is no longer accepting new ride requests from the general public for any period of time as a result of a decision by Tesla to suspend operations in the area, and such suspension is not explicitly characterized as temporary (e.g., due to weather, maintenance, or system upgrades). The Payout Criterion is not satisfied by short-term service interruptions that are clearly communicated as temporary or expected to resume.

The following do NOT satisfy the Payout Criterion:

If a government orders Tesla to cease ongoing services but they do not comply, then the market does not resolve to Yes
Services limited to Tesla employees, contractors, or their guests
Beta tests, pilot programs, or demonstrations
Services requiring special invitations, access codes, or pre-approval to use
Vehicles with human safety drivers, monitors, or operators in any seat of the vehicle who can take control
Temporary suspensions due to weather or technical issues
Services operating only with remote human teleoperators controlling each vehicle continuously
Test fleets that are not charging fares to the general public
Announcements of future launches without actual operational service

The service must be available to the general public without requiring special invitation codes, waitlist approval, or participation in testing programs, though geographic coverage within Tampa, FL may be limited to certain areas. Services operating exclusively with safety drivers present do not satisfy the Payout Criterion; the service must offer fully autonomous rides (without a human safety driver) at least some of the time.

Examples that WOULD resolve to Yes:

Waymo launches public commercial service in any part of Tampa, FL
Waymo expands from adjacent areas into Tampa, FL limits
Waymo operates 24/7 service or limited hours service within Tampa, FL
Waymo offers service through the Uber app to all users in Tampa, FL
Service is geofenced to only certain neighborhoods but is public

Examples that would resolve to No:

Waymo only operates employee shuttles or closed testing in Tampa, FL
Waymo only has an office or maintenance facility in Tampa, FL
All Waymo vehicles in Tampa, FL have safety drivers
Waymo is testing but not offering paid public rides
Service requires being on a waitlist or having a special code
Waymo announces plans to launch but hasn't started service by Jan 1, 2027
